speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you describe what the lesion looks like, how long it has been there, and if it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age, sun exposure, and diabetes, I need to examine the lesion closely; please lift your left hand so I can inspect the area. Are there any changes in size, color, or texture recently, or have you noticed bleeding? REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide a clear photograph of the lesion on your left dorsal hand.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with significant sun exposure is highly characteristic of this pre-malignant lesion caused by cumulative UV radiation. No further tests are required at this time.
